title: Navigating Infertility Together: The Influence of Romantic Attachment on Couple Outcomes—A Systematic Review and Meta‐Analysis
abstract: ABSTRACT Infertility is a significant public health concern, profoundly affecting both individuals and couples. This systematic review and meta‐analysis aims to explore whether romantic attachment serves as a protective or risk factor in how couples navigate infertility diagnoses, treatments, and outcomes, with a specific focus on relational correlates. A systematic search was conducted across six databases from January 1, 2011, to February 3, 2025. Seventeen studies met the inclusion criteria, examining the link between romantic attachment and couple‐related psychological outcomes. Five of these studies were included in a meta‐analysis assessing the associations between attachment anxiety and avoidance and dyadic adjustment. Findings highlight significant associations between insecure attachment dimensions (both anxiety and avoidance) and reduced relationship and sexual satisfaction among individuals facing infertility. Meta‐analytic results revealed moderate negative associations between attachment insecurities and dyadic adjustment. Additionally, cross‐partner effects were observed, indicating that one partner's attachment style can impact the other's infertility experience. This study underscores the pivotal role of romantic attachment in managing infertility‐related challenges, distinguishing the distinct impacts of attachment anxiety and avoidance, and offering valuable clinical insights for supporting couples undergoing fertility treatments.
